method: CRITIC-BRIEF.md + ai-registry/skills/scan-sweep/references/challenge.md §1/§4/§5; every premise and evidence line re-read on the working tree at HEAD eceef19e1 (2026-09-22)

verdicts.title: Make the store's booking collision a real-duration overlap inside the tx
verdicts.premise_notes: All nine lines hold: schedule-store.ts:432 and :557 are `slot_at = ?` equality; duration_min is a per-invite column (:56-59); bookedSlots() (:755-761) returns bare strings; proposeSlots skips only on takenSet.has(value) (schedule-slots.ts:179/194); hourBucketKey's own doc (:338) admits the store would not catch a 14:30 beside a 14:00; its only production caller is app/api/schedule/route.ts:228/231, a read of bookedSlots() before the store call at :257/:264, i.e. outside the transaction; dateSlotToIso accepts any HH:MM (:386). The drained 'Re-check free/busy on accept_proposal and reschedule' is the Google side, not kp's own-booking overlap, so this is not a restatement.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 6, gate contract. 8 files + 1 new test; ~350-450 lines is a fair estimate. Write set is honest: the predicate is pure, the store tx stays synchronous inside .immediate() (the SELECT slot_at, duration_min + bookingCollides is sync, so the no-await rule holds), bookedSlots keeps its string overload so no caller outside the set changes. No catalog, no schema.
verdicts.ambition_why: Moving the collision authority into the lock and deleting the TOCTOU pre-read is the structural fix a principal would make; it stops one notch short of the per-interviewer pool (the open L) but deliberately makes that a key on one predicate.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every claim, including 'one handler of five booking writers' and 'only a connected Google calendar masks it', is exactly what the tree shows.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Six store cases on an isolated KP_DB_PATH plus a pure-predicate case and one route case are all writable before the build against .ts modules, and cases 2 and 7 fail today for the stated reason.

verdicts.title: Turn a revoked Google grant from a silent 'unavailable' into Reconnect now
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. google-calendar.ts:72-74 claims the operator 'sees a disconnected integration' and nothing after it writes; token-store.ts has no health column at all (grep empty) and `connected: !!row.refresh_token` (:99); available-slots.ts:65 folds every connected-but-silent case into 'unavailable'; parseTokenResponse (google-oauth.ts:141-142) only folds Google's error into a message; the Integrations panel's only Reconnect sits inside `missing.length > 0`; ScheduleCalendarStatus offers Connect for not_connected only (:26). CALENDAR_STATUSES is a 3-member literal array pinned to the catalogs by calendar-status-i18n.test.ts, exactly as the card expects. The public token route is 'ONE BIT ONLY' by comment (app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts:160), so 'the candidate wire stays one bit' is true.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 5, gate none. 15 files + 1 new = 16, at the ceiling; two of them (schedule-store.ts, available-slots.ts) are one-function additions. Columns land via ALTER on the existing calendar_connections table, so the tenancy manifest is untouched. 4-locale parity is declared. Not on the leftover list (Meet link / retryCalendarEvent / holidays / interviewer pool / M365) and the two drained CTA items covered not_connected only.
verdicts.ambition_why: A chronic failure rendered as a transient one, with a per-request 8s round trip against a dead grant, is precisely the class a product lead would close; it is the registry's named 'three statuses' move, not a polish.
verdicts.grounding_why: The false comment at :72-74 is the card's strongest exhibit and it is real; every other line matches.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-6 are writable against the .ts calendar modules with a mocked fetch and an isolated DB, and case 7 rides an existing set-equality test; the actionable panel/status renders are .tsx and stay unproven by unit test, which the card admits by not claiming them.

verdicts.title: One application-filing core behind the apply, quick, lead and CV doors
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds at every line. cv-intake.ts:118 `buildApplicantProfile(input.job, answers)` passes no workspaceId while applicant-profile.ts:160-166 documents undefined = default workspace; route.ts:513-520 names that exact defect and fixes its own door only; both CV callers (channels/inbound/[token]/route.ts:153-162, sim/apply-cv/route.ts:72-83) hand in a non-default workspace; findApplicationByApplicant has two callers and cv-intake is not one; cv-intake.ts:112 'Applicant' + apply-intake.ts:126-127 yields 'appl-applicant' while route.ts:243-246 forbids exactly that merge; stage rule x3, consent block x4, status-link mint x2, sanitizeFreeText on lead-intake only - all verified.
verdicts.floor_notes: L, effort 8, impact 8, risk 7, gate architecture (allowed on the deck). 8 files, 2 new. Line estimate is at the upper edge: ~300 new core + ~250 removed from the 649-line route + two wrappers + docs is roughly 700-900 changed lines; the card should be held to it. Write set is honest because ingestCvApplication/intakeLead keep their exported types, so the four external callers stay untouched - except that acceptance 1 requires an injectable builder, which means ingestCvApplication's input type grows an optional field (still inside cv-intake.ts). Not on the leftover list; the open L 'resume token' is a different idea and is named as B's runner-up, not here.
verdicts.ambition_why: Three live defects (tenant split, orphan profile, anonymous collapse) and four copies collapsed into one core that every future door inherits is the move a principal makes; the runner-up (CAS-guarded intake command) was correctly traded away as the smaller seam.
verdicts.grounding_why: The card's most consequential claim - a real cross-tenant split on the inbound CV channel - is exactly what the tree does today.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-3 and 7 fail today for demonstrable reasons and are writable against .ts modules with an injected builder and KP_DB_PATH; case 5's 'exactly one consent event' is loose on the proven-merge path (today the merge re-consents on top of the original, so the count is 2 - the builder must read it as one NEW event per filing).

verdicts.title: Turn 'already applied' into link recovery sent to the address on file
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. route.ts:412-414 promises the re-send; :415-421 only links the funnel session and returns acknowledgeReapply with no dispatch; :130 records re_applied only when proven while en.json:2233 says 'We've noted your renewed interest'; quick/route.ts:194-200 answers a duplicate with nothing but the message; ApplyDoneCard.tsx:31/:45 leave an unproven duplicate with no action; dispatchApplicationReceived already renders enrich+status links (comms-dispatch.ts:348-366); sendCandidateComm mints a refused 'failed' row on a null recipient (:286-301); login-throttle exports isThrottled/recordFailedAttempt and invite/[token] uses them per key (:47-53); the resend grep finds only the recruiter-side door. reapply-capability-gate.test.ts:108-153 pins the unproven path with a null-contact victim, as the card says.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 5, gate contract. 10 files + 2 new; ~350-450 lines. Catalog parity declared (5 new keys x 4). No new table: the cooldown reuses login_throttle under a new key prefix. The bounded griefing vector (one mail per entry per day, to the victim's own address, carrying only their own links) is stated, not hidden. The drained 'Make a quick-apply decline recoverable in place' is the decline path, not the duplicate path.
verdicts.ambition_why: It makes the route's own promise true and removes a dead end on the most common re-apply path without loosening the capability gate - the right product move, though it is one branch on two routes rather than a structural change.

verdicts.title: Make relay capability a live fact the relay editor invalidates, not a boot cache
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. useDeliveryCapability.ts:5-7 states the 'server restart' premise; :33-34 `let cached`/`let inflight`; :60 `if (cached !== null) return;`; only the two hooks are exported; comms-relay.ts:3-5 says the relay is UI-configurable and resolve() reads the store per call; POST /api/comms/relay stores at runtime; ChannelsRelayConfigCard.save() re-reads its own config on ok and 409 and calls neither an invalidation nor notifyDataChanged (grep: only ChannelsCvSimCard calls it); ChannelsCommsTable seeds relayConfigured true and re-reads only on useLiveRefresh; 11 consumer files confirmed by grep; live-refresh.ts (88 lines) posts the literal 'changed' with no topic.
verdicts.floor_notes: Declared M / effort 6 / impact 8 / risk 5, gate contract, 4 files + 3 new. Honest estimate: ~120 lines of store, ~150 of tests, ~30 of hook rewire, 6 lines in the relay card - an M-lite of ~300 lines. Effort 6 and impact 8 are inflated (a relay is saved a handful of times per install; the lie lasts until a reload); this card sits on the M floor rather than above it. Not on the leftover list.
verdicts.ambition_why: An invalidatable cache with a generation guard is the correct fix and a small one - it is a stabilize-loop item dressed as a challenge; the runner-up (one write-only endpoint-config hook for the twin relay/edge cards, before a third copy lands for pull sources) was the more structural seam and was the one to bring.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every line, count and grep result is as stated, including the 'server restart' comment that is false on its own tab.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Seven pure store cases with an injected fetcher and channel stub are writable first against a DOM-free .ts module; case 8 is a source assertion over a .tsx file, which is readable but proves presence, not behaviour.

Adopts the open leftover 'Add a pull-source editor on each receiver row' (candidate-channels-ui, M, i9, r3) explicitly, and it is absent from both drain results files - allowed under §3. verdicts.title: Put the fit grid on the shared tier scale and carry the scorer's band per cell
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. fit-thresholds.ts:13/:23 = 55/70 mirrored to matching.py:80-81 by test_fit_threshold_sync.py; matrixStats.ts:19 `min: 72`, :24 STRONG_THRESHOLD = 72, :31 MIN_FIT_FLOORS = [0,45,72]; useMatrixTab.ts:308 and :353-354 count strong at 72; MatchCard.tsx:100 renders FitTierBadge and Badge.tsx:263 bands at FIT_STRONG_FLOOR; matrix_cli.py:113 keeps only `.total` (grep for confidence/fitTier/unproven: 0 hits) while MatchResult carries confidence (:276) and unproven_skills (:291); route.ts:20-28 declares four optional fields nothing emits and matrix-cell.test.ts:1-4 admits it. One thing the card does NOT cite: matrixStats.ts:27-30 records the CURRENT derivation (floors from bands, 72) as a deliberate earlier fix that replaced [0,55,70] because '>=70 survived rows the grid renders non-strong'. The card reverses that recorded decision - defensibly, since it re-bands the grid so the floors and bands agree at the shared edges - but it should say so. test_matrix_cli.py:85-87 pins only the blocked-cell shape and `score` as int, so adding keys to a scored cell does not break it.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 6, gate contract. 11 files, none new; ~300-400 lines across TS and Python. MATRIX_BANDS labels ('45-59', '60-71', '72-84') are hardcoded strings that must be regenerated with the edges - inside matrixStats.ts, so no growth. The open leftover 'Paint cell confidence and unproven on the fit grid' is not restated: this card ships the wire and re-bands, and paints nothing new.
verdicts.ambition_why: One fit scale across the tab and the app, with the coverage banner no longer wrong at the tier edge, plus the honesty fields finally on the wire, is a principal's move; it is a parity fix at heart rather than a new capability.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited line is true, but the card omits that matrixStats.ts:27-30 documents the opposite derivation as deliberate, so the builder must reverse a recorded decision it was not told about.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Numeric equalities (STRONG_THRESHOLD === 70, columnStats([69,70,71]).strong === 2), a tier-edge invariant, a source-reading declared-vs-emitted test and a Python payload test all fail today and are writable first.

MatrixGridRow.tsx:87 renders the star count as the only allocation signal; :103 `inPipe = place && !isTerminalEntryStatus(place.status)`; useMatrixTab.ts:484-509 files every ticked key in sequence with no per-candidate or per-role grouping; :350-357 coverage names uncovered roles and proposes nobody; matrixSelection.ts:58-67 visibleMatrixCellKeys; MatrixSelectBar.tsx:41-45 discloses hidden selections; MatrixTab.tsx:182-220 reports partial failure; FIT_PROMISING_FLOOR = 55; grep for slate/contested/allocat in the matrix folder: 0 hits.

verdicts.title: One throwable Refusal + answerFailure: lib errors carry the code, not routes
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. jsonRefusal (api-response.ts:1890) and safeJsonError (:1923) are unjoined; AtsConnectionError (connections-store.ts:46-56), AtsFieldMapError (field-map.ts:129-139) and PortabilityError (db-portability.ts:25-34) are three hand-made code-carrying shapes; PostingClosedError (distribution.ts:97-102) carries no code and three devcase routes re-type `jsonRefusal("POSTING_CLOSED", 410)`; export/import routes repeat the PortabilityError branch and import-body-limit.test.ts:68 pins it by regex; ats/connections/route.ts:77-80 re-derives the split; MatrixAnswer and ExtractAnswer are two more classifiers; counts reproduce (30 distinct instanceof checks, 39 non-test files declaring an Error subclass); jobs/[id]/candidates/route.ts:99-100 forwards PipelineError.message. AtsConnectionStaleError already extends AtsConnectionError (:61-66), consistent with the card. The one flaw is a design claim, not a premise: REFUSAL_ERRORS is defined in api-response.ts (:519), whose first line imports next/server. A Refusal whose default `.message` is `REFUSAL_ERRORS[code]` (case 1) must import that map at runtime, so 'any lib module can throw it without pulling NextResponse' (case 7) is only true as a direct-import source assertion, not transitively - and the card explicitly declines to move the catalogs.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 6, impact 8, risk 5, gate architecture (allowed on the deck). 13 files + 2 new = 15; ~350-450 lines. Wire shape unchanged, so no catalog change. Distinct from the pending 'Split the STORE_ERRORS / REFUSAL_ERRORS catalogs' item as the card says.
verdicts.ambition_why: Classify once at the throw site and route once at the door, with a tree guard so the pattern cannot fork again, is the right structural move over 30 instanceof branches; the runner-up (validated request-body door over 117 raw request.json() callers) is arguably bigger and was traded away.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited line and count is true; the 'no next/server' property is overstated because the default message needs a map that lives beside NextResponse.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-6 are pure and writable against refusal.ts/api-response.ts before the build; case 7 as written passes trivially on a direct-import assertion while the property it names is false, so it would not catch the wrong build it exists for.
verdicts.revise: Case 1: make Refusal's default `.message` the code string itself (or a caller-supplied detail), NOT `REFUSAL_ERRORS[code]` - that map is defined in app/_lib/api-response.ts:519, whose line 1 imports next/server, so the only way to keep case 7's 'no NextResponse pull' honest is for refusal.ts to import only the `RefusalErrorCode` type from api-response (type imports erase) and nothing at runtime; answerFailure in api-response.ts then resolves REFUSAL_ERRORS[code] for the wire, where it already lives.

verdicts.title: Limiter refusals that say when: shared Retry-After from the window's own state
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. rate-limit.ts:13 `type Window = { count; resetAt }`, :21-35 returns a bare boolean and discards resetAt; exactly 147 non-test `jsonRefusal("TOO_MANY_REQUESTS", 429)` sites; exactly 4 Retry-After setters (login:55, invite:42, stt:77, tts:53), login and invite carrying the same clamp verbatim; tts/route.ts:42-50 explains the contract-test pin; rate-limit-contract.test.ts:2146-2159 checks the 400 chars after the limiter call; the five machine doors are refused with no header at the cited lines; ops/route.ts:122-126 exposes in-process counters with no limiter counter; leftover line 590 is the adopted item and it is absent from both drain results files.

Adopts an open M item (r2, i9) explicitly and widens it with the tree rule and the ops counter - allowed under §3. rate-limit-contract.test.ts is declared a shared surface, correctly.
verdicts.ambition_why: A truthful Retry-After from the arithmetic that refused, one clamp instead of four, and a refusal counter is solid platform hygiene; it is a widened backlog item rather than a seam only a principal would see, and the runner-up (a behavioural route driver to retire 58 source-regex contract tests) was the more ambitious card.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every count reproduces exactly (147 / 4 / 30-something contract lines) and the pin's rationale is quoted from the tree.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: The window read, clamp, jsonThrottled body and refusal-stats cases are pure and numeric; the tree rule is a source scan; case 5's behavioural drive of five doors depends on those route modules being importable under node:test (billing/webhook and agents/report carry heavy graphs), which the tree does not yet demonstrate.

verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. tasks.ts:201 `const HANDLERS: Record<string, Spec> = {` with 20 kinds; task-budget.test.ts:25-27 and task-outcome-summary.test.ts:28-32 both readFileSync tasks.ts and regex `^ {2}([a-z_]+): \{$`; tasks-pump.test.ts:77 finds the same literal and :108 matches an indentation-dependent tenancy regex (and :106 asserts `blocks.size >= 17`, which the builder must retarget - inside the write set); task-dedupe.test.ts has zero readFileSync/HANDLERS references, so dedupe has no exhaustiveness check; task-dedupe.ts:80 Record<string,...> with profile_draft's opt-out as a comment (:168); task-budget.ts:59 Record<string,...> and :113 `?? "agent"`; TABLE/NO_TABLE_SUMMARY are string-keyed; tasksProviderTypes.ts:38 `kind: string`; exactly 25 literal startTask sites; api/tasks/route.ts:57 isKnownKind is the only check and is `boolean`, not a predicate; task-external-runners.ts:22-28 documents intake_round outside the queue. Server-side callers outside the set (companion-actions x2, jd-build-start, repo-scan, jobseeker/scan via `SCAN_TASK_KIND = "jobseeker_scan"`) all pass literal-typed values, so retyping startTask does not grow the write set.

verdicts.ambition_why: It is the repo's own closed-vocabulary pattern applied to the one registry still held together by source regexes - a class-closing tidy-up a principal would approve, but the runner-up (a pure planPass so the dry-run and commit loops cannot diverge) was the structural seam of this context.

verdicts.title: Fan-out tasks report per-candidate outcomes and retry only the failed
verdicts.premise_notes: Holds. tasks.ts:190-191 pushes `{ id, ok: true }` on any non-throwing return while automation-run.ts:721/:729-733 return already_sent / suppressed_* without throwing; :193 stores `reason: e.message` raw although AutomationError carries a `refusal` code (:169-183); batchScreen's catch is `summary.errors += 1` (:145-147); the drawer renders 'drafted ok / total' (task-outcome-summary.ts:166-172) and an errors count (TasksOutcome.tsx:47-49); retry is gated to failed/interrupted/canceled (TasksRowActions.tsx:66, retry/route.ts:23) and replays full params (:100); a canceled run stores its partial result (:666); usePipelineBulk.ts:458-463 is the only keep-the-failures path; tasks is erasure-exempt and not entry-keyed (db/pipeline.ts:2198); batch_outreach dedupes on the sorted cohort (task-dedupe.ts:107-111). No test file exists under api/tasks/[id]/retry. Also verified: NO test in the tree imports app/_lib/tasks.ts at runtime - the three existing task tests all parse its source text instead - so cases 6-8, which import retry/route.ts (which imports startTask from tasks.ts), would be the first, and their writability is unproven.
verdicts.floor_notes: M, effort 7, impact 8, risk 5, gate contract. 12 files + 3 new = 15; ~500-650 lines with four catalogs. Result shape is additive, the retry body field is optional, no table added, ids-and-codes only (erasure posture preserved). Heavy overlap with task A (7 shared files) - see overlaps; A changes startTask's signature and must run alone and first.
verdicts.ambition_why: A drawer that over-claims delivery becoming a per-candidate, coded, subset-retryable decision surface is a real elevation aligned with the product's truthful-delivery rule; the runner-up (commit exactly the previewed policy pass) is of similar weight.
verdicts.grounding_why: The over-claim at tasks.ts:190-191 against automation-run.ts:729-733 is exactly as described, and the raw-message write at :193 is a live violation of the house CODE rule.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-5 are pure and writable against task-fanout.ts before the build; cases 6-8 require importing the retry route, which pulls tasks.ts and its handler graph into node:test for the first time in this tree - if that import does not boot cleanly the three route cases cannot be written before the implementation.
verdicts.revise: Cases 6-8: express the retry decision as a pure `retryDecision(task, scope)` in task-fanout.ts (status + stored result + params -> {ok: subset params} | {refuse: 'TASK_NOT_RETRYABLE'} | {refuse: 'TASK_NOT_FOUND'}) and write the three cases against it, keeping the route as a thin caller; do not make the route test file (app/api/tasks/[id]/retry/route.test.ts) an acceptance case, since no test in the tree imports app/_lib/tasks.ts at runtime today and the tenancy/404-before-limiter ordering can be asserted on the pure function's input order.

overlaps.note: A rewrites the duplicate branches B wires into; A must land first and B re-verify its line numbers
A extracts uncoveredRoles from the coverage memo B's slate reads beside
A collapses the catch block, B rewrites the two limiter refusals above it
A retypes HANDLERS and startTask (a signature other cards call: run ALONE, first); B rewrites the batchScreen/batchOutreach bodies
declared shared_surfaces on every card that touches them; the §7 lock handles this, it does not break wave disjointness

summary.note: Every A/B pair in the cohort shares at least one source file, so the six contexts yield at most six disjoint builders per wave (one slot each), not twelve; task A must run alone because it changes startTask's signature.
